cureTechnologies.name: Platinum-Cure Liquid Silicone Rubber (LSR) – Factory Tempered
cureTechnologies.catalyst: Karstedt Platinum Complex (Pt 10–20 ppm, Hydrosilylation Addition Cure)
cureTechnologies.postCureTempering: Tempered (4 hours at 200°C in circulating hot air oven)
cureTechnologies.pinchTestBehavior: Colorfast (Zero whitening; 100% pure cross-linked polydimethylsiloxane network)
cureTechnologies.thermalBreakdownCharacteristics: Extremely stable Si-O-Si siloxane backbone; negligible depolymerization up to 260°C. Virtually zero volatile organic acid emissions.
cureTechnologies.description: Medical and premium culinary grade platinum-cure silicone. Fully tempered post-cure in commercial hot-air tunnels to purge all residual low-molecular-weight cyclic oligomers before consumer packaging.

cureTechnologies.name: Platinum-Cure Silicone – Untempered / Economy Grade
cureTechnologies.catalyst: Platinum Addition Cure (Factory Skipped Post-Cure Tempering to Cut Energy Costs)
cureTechnologies.bfrRecommendationXvStatus: Non-Compliant (>0.5% VOM threshold exceeded on first 3 bakes)
cureTechnologies.fda1772600Status: Borderline / Initial Exceedance (>4.0 mg/sq inch without pre-wash bake)
cureTechnologies.pinchTestBehavior: Colorfast (Does not turn white; pure silicone matrix, but saturated with unvented volatile oligomers)
cureTechnologies.thermalBreakdownCharacteristics: Heavy outgassing of cyclic siloxanes (D4–D8) during first 1–3 heating cycles above 180°C. Releases noticeable 'hot silicone' vapor plume into oven cavity.
cureTechnologies.description: Mid-tier bakeware that utilizes genuine platinum catalysis but omits the expensive 4-hour factory tempering cycle. Requires an initial consumer burn-off bake at 200°C in a well-ventilated room before food contact.

cureTechnologies.name: Peroxide-Cure High Consistency Rubber (HCR)
cureTechnologies.catalyst: Organic Peroxides (2,4-Dichlorobenzoyl Peroxide / DBPH Free-Radical Cure)
cureTechnologies.bfrRecommendationXvStatus: Violates BfR XV (<0.5% VOM and <10 mg/dm² migration breached)
cureTechnologies.fda1772600Status: Fails FDA Repeated-Use Fatty Food Extraction without prolonged tempering
cureTechnologies.pinchTestBehavior: Faint Whitening (Minor structural micro-stretching; low-density crosslink density)
cureTechnologies.thermalBreakdownCharacteristics: Thermally degrades above 200°C. Free-radical decomposition leaves residual 2,4-dichlorobenzoic acid and volatile organic acid traces, emitting an acrid, sweet-chemical odor on heating.
cureTechnologies.description: Older commercial rubber manufacturing process. Peroxide curing leaves volatile crosslinking byproducts and high concentrations of cyclic oligomers (D3–D10) that readily leach into hot oils and molten fats.

cureTechnologies.name: Adulterated Silicone with Mineral Fillers & Hydrocarbon Plasticizers
cureTechnologies.catalyst: Low-Grade Peroxide or Unknown Industrial Cure + Chalk/Talc/Oil Extenders
cureTechnologies.postCureTempering: Zero Tempering (Contains up to 35% non-silicone adulterants)
cureTechnologies.bfrRecommendationXvStatus: Hazardous / Total Regulatory Failure (Extreme migration >40 mg/dm²)
cureTechnologies.fda1772600Status: Illegal for Food Contact (Massive chemical migration into lipid matrices)
cureTechnologies.pinchTestBehavior: Immediate Stark White (Severe micro-cavitation and light scattering around mineral filler granules)
cureTechnologies.thermalBreakdownCharacteristics: Severe thermal breakdown above 180°C. Hydrocarbon plasticizers smoke and pyrolyze; silicone rapidly discolors to yellow/brown, stiffens, develops micro-cracks, and sheds particulates.
cureTechnologies.description: Counterfeit and ultra-cheap kitchenware sold on bargain marketplaces. Manufacturers blend silicone resin with cheap calcium carbonate (chalk), talc, and industrial process oils to reduce raw material costs by 60%.

foodMatrices.name: High-Fat Baked Goods & Butter Pastry (>20% Fat)
foodMatrices.solubilityMechanism: Non-polar cyclic siloxanes (D4, D5, D6) possess extreme lipophilic affinity (log Kow ~5.1–8.8). Hot molten butter, vegetable oils, and cocoa butter act as aggressive extraction solvents pulling oligomers across the polymer boundary.
foodMatrices.description: Pound cake, croissants, brioche, shortbread, and chocolate brownies. Hot lipids penetrate the micro-porous silicone surface and dissolve free siloxane rings rapidly.

foodMatrices.name: Savory Meat, Poultry & Rendered Animal Tallow (>30% Fat)
foodMatrices.solubilityMechanism: Rendered liquid animal fats at roasting temperatures (>200°C) achieve near-complete surface wetting and lipid extraction. Siloxane migration is highest under prolonged thermal fat immersion.
foodMatrices.description: Meatloaf, bacon, roast chicken, and pork sausages baked in silicone loaf pans or roasting mats.

foodMatrices.name: Acidic Fruit Cakes & Lemon / Berry Batters (pH 3.0–4.0)
foodMatrices.solubilityMechanism: Organic fruit acids (citric, malic, tartaric) catalyze siloxane depolymerization (Si-O bond hydrolysis) at temperatures above 180°C, accelerating cyclic oligomer regeneration.
foodMatrices.description: Lemon drizzle cakes, berry muffins, tomato tarts, and rhubarb crumbles.

foodMatrices.name: Lean Bread Dough & Pizza Crust (<5% Fat)
foodMatrices.solubilityMechanism: Aqueous starch gel matrix. Cyclic siloxanes have virtually zero water solubility (<50 µg/L); migration into lean bread dough is limited purely to superficial boundary adhesion.
foodMatrices.description: Sourdough baguettes, artisan boules, pizza crusts, and yeast dinner rolls with minimal shortening.

foodMatrices.name: Sub-Ambient Chocolate, Gelatin & Ice Mold (-20°C to 20°C)
foodMatrices.solubilityMechanism: Zero thermal activation. At ambient and freezer temperatures, molecular mobility of PDMS polymer chains is virtually frozen; chemical migration is below detectable analytical limits (<0.01 mg/dm²).
foodMatrices.description: Freezer ice cube trays, chocolate bonbon molds, gummy candy molds, and cold-set cheesecakes.

oligomerProfiles.name: Octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane
oligomerProfiles.regulatoryClassification: EU REACH SVHC (Substance of Very High Concern) • Toxic to Reproduction (Repr. Cat 2) • PBT/vPvB
oligomerProfiles.toxicologicalImpact: Endocrine disruption (weak estrogenic activity); bioaccumulates in adipose lipid tissues. Inhalation of volatilized D4 in unventilated kitchens induces respiratory tract irritation.
oligomerProfiles.volatilizationBehavior: Volatilizes aggressively above 175°C (347°F), condensing onto oven heating coils, glass doors, and food surfaces.

oligomerProfiles.name: Decamethylcyclopentasiloxane
oligomerProfiles.regulatoryClassification: EU REACH Annex XVII Restricted • Very Persistent and Very Bioaccumulative (vPvB)
oligomerProfiles.toxicologicalImpact: Extremely resistant to biological and environmental breakdown; accumulates in human fatty tissues and aquatic food chains.
oligomerProfiles.volatilizationBehavior: Starts outgassing moderately at 190°C; reaches peak volatilization between 210°C and 230°C.

oligomerProfiles.name: Dodecamethylcyclohexasiloxane
oligomerProfiles.regulatoryClassification: EU REACH SVHC Candidate • Very Persistent, Very Bioaccumulative (vPvB)
oligomerProfiles.toxicologicalImpact: High lipid solubility; long biological elimination half-life in mammalian liver and fat reserves.
oligomerProfiles.volatilizationBehavior: Low room-temperature volatility, but migrates directly into hot food oils above 200°C.

temperatureRiskTiers.safetySummary: Completely safe for all food types across all genuine silicone grades. No significant cyclic siloxane mobilization.

temperatureRiskTiers.outgassingSeverity: Mild outgassing in unbaked new molds
temperatureRiskTiers.safetySummary: Safe for tempered platinum silicone. Peroxide molds release minor cyclic siloxanes into butter-rich crusts.

temperatureRiskTiers.outgassingSeverity: Strong volatile siloxane outgassing; noticeable odor from untempered silicone
temperatureRiskTiers.safetySummary: BfR 0.5% volatile threshold frequently exceeded by economy and peroxide siloxanes. High-fat pastries extract significant D4/D5.

temperatureRiskTiers.outgassingSeverity: Dense outgassing; thermal backbone depolymerization initiates
temperatureRiskTiers.safetySummary: Chain scission produces new low-molecular-weight siloxanes. Adulterated filler molds smoke, char, and turn brittle.

temperatureRiskTiers.outgassingSeverity: Smoke, white silica (SiO2) aerosol ash, and trace formaldehyde emissions
temperatureRiskTiers.safetySummary: Exceeds structural thermal limit of PDMS elastomer. Rapid polymer breakdown; potential toxic combustion byproducts.
